body.statement: Fix algebraic \(s\), \(\kappa\), count cutoff, and endpoint grid. On each smooth semialgebraic target-membership and nuisance-boundary stratum, every coverage or saved-length surface for a fixed action profile has the form \(\exp\{-\kappa M(\eta)\}p_a(\eta)\), and every interior critical point satisfies \(dp_a-\kappa p_a\,dM=0\) on the stratum tangent space. Finitely many connected critical components contain every extremal value, and outward algebraic--exponential enclosures decide every strict rational coverage or risk comparison.
body.justification: This gives concrete fixed-design traction and isolates the remaining difficulty as uniform parameterization of contacts over shares and intensity.
body.gap: Generic real-algebraic optimization does not directly decide exponential coverage surfaces; the cancellation in the critical equations is specific to the fixed-design Poisson likelihood.
body.consumer: Verified solvers can replace arbitrary nuisance sampling by finite critical-component enclosures at each algebraic design.
